name: Charles Schwab
description: Schwab is the largest US retail brokerage and holds $11.9 trillion of client assets (Dec 31, 2025). It serves individual investors directly and independent financial advisors who custody their clients' money at Schwab. It makes money four ways: the gap between interest earned on client cash and securities (invested mainly through its Charles Schwab Bank) and what it pays out, which was 49% of 2025 net revenue; fees on managed portfolios and its own funds and ETFs (27%); trading revenue including payment for order flow and margin-related activity (16%); and bank deposit account fees paid by its bank sweep program (4%). Growth depends on gathering new client assets ($498.6B net new in 2025) and on interest rates, since client cash earns Schwab a spread.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge, not re-checked. SEC SIC code is 6211 (Security Brokers, Dealers & Flotation Companies). Half of revenue is interest income, earned mostly through its bank, so it behaves like a bank on client cash.

hq.note: From general knowledge; cover page not re-read in this pass.

employees.note: Full-time equivalent, including part-time, temporary and contract workers (10-K)

businessLines.name: Investor Services
businessLines.how: Spread on uninvested client cash and margin loans, fees on advisory portfolios and Schwab funds, and per-trade related revenue; clients are individuals paying little or nothing in trade commissions.
businessLines.description: Retail investors served directly: brokerage, banking, trading, retirement business services and Schwab's own funds.

businessLines.name: Advisor Services
businessLines.how: The advisor charges the end client; Schwab earns the cash spread, fees on assets and trading revenue for providing custody and platform access.
businessLines.description: Custody, trading and support for independent registered investment advisors and their clients.
